create_board.description: Create a board on the connected Pinterest account and answer with it, including the id later steps read, rename, section or delete it by. A board can be public, protected (visible only to people you share it with) or secret; public unless you say otherwise.

mock_response.description: Things to cook when it is too hot to cook.
mock_response.name: Summer recipes

create_board.name: create_board

parameters.description: The board's name, shown on your profile.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: Optional. What the board is for.
parameters.name: description

parameters.description: Who can see the board. Public by default. Protected boards are visible only to people you share them with; secret boards only to you.
parameters.name: privacy

board_pins_modified_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last change to its contents.

collaborator_count.description: How many people may add to this board.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the board was created.

follower_count.description: How many people follow the board.

id.description: Unique board id, a string of digits.

is_ads_only.description: Whether the board can hold only ad-only content.

pin_thumbnail_urls.description: Thumbnail addresses of the board's contents.

owner.description: The account that owns the board.

pin_count.description: How many items the board holds.

create_board_section.description: Add a section to a board (the named groups Pinterest shows as tiles at the top of a board) and answer with it, including the id later steps rename or delete it by.
create_board_section.display_str_template: Create the section '{1}' on Pinterest board {0}.

parameters.description: Which board to act on. The list holds the boards this account owns and the group boards it collaborates on; you can also paste a board id (a string of digits) that an earlier step produced. parameters.description: The section's name, up to 180 characters.
parameters.name: name

returns.description: A section of a board: a named group inside it.

delete_board.description: Permanently remove a board from the connected Pinterest account, together with everything saved on it. This cannot be undone, so read the board first if you need a copy.
delete_board.name: delete_board

returns.description: Confirmation that the record was removed.

get_account_analytics.description: Read how the whole connected account performed over a date range: impressions, clicks, outbound clicks, saves, engagement and their rates, day by day and as a summary. Pinterest keeps the last 90 days, and a range may cover at most 90 days. An account with no activity in the range legitimately reports nothing, which the result flags rather than failing.
get_account_analytics.display_str_template: Get Pinterest account analytics from {0} to {1}.
get_account_analytics.name: get_account_analytics

parameters.description: First day of the report, in UTC. Pinterest keeps the last 90 days only, so this cannot be further back than that.
parameters.name: start_date

parameters.description: Last day of the report, in UTC. It must be on or after the From date and no more than 90 days past it.
parameters.name: end_date

parameters.description: Optional. Which figures to report. Choose none for all of them.
parameters.name: metric_types

parameters.description: Optional. Count content from websites you have claimed, content from anywhere else, or both. Both by default.
parameters.name: from_claimed_content

parameters.description: Optional. Count only one format of content. All formats by default.
parameters.name: pin_format

parameters.description: Optional. Count only activity from this kind of device. All devices by default.
parameters.name: app_types

parameters.description: Optional. Count paid activity, organic activity, or both. Both by default.
parameters.name: content_type

parameters.description: Optional. Count only your own content, only content others created from your site, or both. Both by default.
parameters.name: source

parameters.description: Optional. Report separate figures per device, per owned/unowned content, per source or per content format. One combined report by default; a broken-down one arrives under 'results', keyed by the split.
parameters.name: split_field

returns.description: One analytics report. Pinterest answers with a map keyed by the split that was asked for, so the whole map is kept under 'results' and the single (or 'ALL') split is lifted out for convenience.

daily_metrics.description: One entry per day in the requested range.

data_status.description: Per-metric readiness, for example READY, PROCESSING or ESTIMATE. A day that is not READY is not a failure.

date.description: The day these metrics cover (UTC), as YYYY-MM-DD.

metrics.description: Metric name to value, for example IMPRESSION, PIN_CLICK, SAVE, OUTBOUND_CLICK, SAVE_RATE. Which names appear depends on the metrics that were asked for.

end_date.description: The last day of the range that was asked for.

is_empty.description: True when Pinterest reported no figures at all for the range. An account with no activity in the range legitimately has none — it is not a failure.

lifetime_metrics.description: All-time totals. Empty when Pinterest reports none.

results.description: Pinterest's report exactly as it sent it, keyed by split. Read this when more than one split was asked for.

splits.description: The keys Pinterest's report is divided by. One entry when no split was asked for.

start_date.description: The first day of the range that was asked for.

summary_metrics.description: Metric name to value, for example IMPRESSION, PIN_CLICK, SAVE, OUTBOUND_CLICK, SAVE_RATE. Which names appear depends on the metrics that were asked for.
